v.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 2 is off the live path (bottleneck) and adds nothing.
Node 1 is dead when edge 0 is none, so a stronger op on edge 4 carries no signal.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct input-to-output path adds a whole new path, which gives more gain than upgrading an existing op.
A skip already supplies a clean direct path, so replacing it with a conv gains less (redundancy) than filling an empty edge.
Upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 is a smaller step than replacing a weak op such as none or pooling, so the gain is lower.
A strong direct conv path to the output already exists, so another conv feeding the output is partly redundant and the parent has less room to improve.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 only reaches the output through nothing, so edge 1 is off the output path and its upgrade is wasted.
With edge 4 gone, node 1 can only reach the output through edge 2 and edge 5, so edge 0's upgrade passes through fewer paths.
Removing edge 4 costs little when a strong direct conv on edge 3 already feeds the output (redundancy), so the drop is smaller.
Replacing a strong conv with pooling loses far more than replacing a weak op, so the edit is much more harmful.

**Eight default assumptions and their negations** 1. Assumption: Adding a conv (3x3) helps regardless of context. Negation: its gain depends on the parent. If the target edge already has a strong parallel path, the gain shrinks. 2. Assumption: A direct input-to-output skip (edge 3 = skip_connect) is always mildly helpful. Negation: with conv paths already present it adds little, so extra convs are diluted. 3. Assumption: Replacing none with an op always helps. Negation: when the output is already fed by a strong direct path, a new feeder adds little or hurts. 4. Assumption: A stronger parent leaves the edit's gain unchanged. Negation: strong parents leave less room, so the same edit gives less. 5. Assumption: Pooling is a harmless filler. Negation: when it replaces a conv, it loses much more. 6. Assumption: Removing an edge (none) is bad. Negation: it is nearly harmless when that edge is redundant with a parallel path. 7. Assumption: Edges are independent. Negation: an upstream edge set to none makes downstream edges bottlenecked (irrelevant). 8. Assumption: conv1x1 and conv3x3 are interchangeable. Negation: upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 helps less when the parent is already conv-rich elsewhere, but more when it replaces a weak op. **Hypotheses kept (mechanism-supported)** - Bottleneck: an edit on edge 5 matters more when edge 1 or edge 2 is not none (the path exists). Edits on edge 2 matter less if edge 0 and edge 1 are none, which is rare, so I use edge 0 = none. - Redundancy: a conv added on edge 4 or 5 is diluted when edge 3 is already a conv. - Parent quality: edits that make a conv are worth less when the replaced op is already a conv, and more when it replaces none.
